metadata.title: Regularization of Neural Networks using DropConnect
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: DropConnect Network
nodes.statement: Given dataset $S$ with $\ell$ entries $\{x_1,\dots,x_\ell\}$ with labels $\{y_1,\dots,y_\ell\}$, the DropConnect network is the mixture model $o = \sum_M p(M) f(x;\theta,M) = E_M[f(x;\theta,M)]$, with parameters $\theta=\{W_s,W,W_g\}$ and binary mask $M$.
nodes.statement_clean: A DropConnect network is a mixture over binary weight masks $M$ that produces predictions by averaging the masked subnetworks.

nodes.name: Logistic Loss
nodes.statement: For $k$-class classification, $A_y(o) = -\sum_i y_i \ln \frac{\exp o_i}{\sum_j \exp o_j} = -o_i + \ln \sum_j \exp(o_j)$, where $y$ is a binary vector with the $i$-th bit set on.
nodes.statement_clean: Logistic loss combines softmax output with one-hot labels into a single scalar loss.

nodes.name: Empirical Rademacher Complexity
nodes.statement: For sample $S=\{x_1,\dots,x_\ell\}$ from distribution $D$ and real-valued function class $F$ on $X$, $\hat R_\ell(F) = E_\sigma\left[\sup_{f\in F} \frac{2}{\ell} \left|\sum_{i=1}^\ell \sigma_i f(x_i)\right| \mid x_1,\dots,x_\ell\right]$, with $\sigma_i$ independent uniform $\{\pm 1\}$ random variables.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard empirical Rademacher complexity of a function class.

nodes.name: Dropout Layer
nodes.statement: Dropout applied to a fully connected layer's output: $r = m \star a(W v)$, where $\star$ is element-wise product and $m_j \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)$ independently for each unit $j$.
nodes.statement_clean: Dropout zeros each output activation independently with probability $1-p$.

nodes.name: DropConnect Layer
nodes.statement: DropConnect layer output: $r = a((M \star W) v)$ where $M$ is a binary mask matrix with $M_{ij} \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)$, drawn independently per training example.
nodes.statement_clean: DropConnect drops individual connections (entries of $W$) independently rather than whole units.

nodes.name: Full DropConnect Model Architecture
nodes.statement: Composed of: feature extractor $v=g(x;W_g)$ (CNN), DropConnect layer $r=a((M\star W)v)$, softmax classifier $o=s(r;W_s)$, and cross-entropy loss $A(y,o)=-\sum_{i=1}^k y_i \log(o_i)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Four-component architecture: CNN feature extractor, DropConnect layer, softmax, cross-entropy loss.

nodes.name: Mixture Output via Mask Marginalization
nodes.statement: $o = E_M[f(x;\theta,M)] = \sum_M p(M) f(x;\theta,M)$ — the exact output sums over all $2^{|M|}$ masks.

nodes.name: Gaussian Moment Matching for $u$
nodes.statement: For $u_i = \sum_j (W_{ij} v_j) M_{ij}$: $E_M[u] = p W v$ and $V_M[u] = p(1-p) (W \star W)(v \star v)$, approximated as Gaussian.

nodes.name: Generalization Bound (Eqn 5)
nodes.statement: $\hat R_\ell(F) \le p \cdot 2 \sqrt{k} d B_s n \sqrt{d} B_h \hat R_\ell(G)$ — Rademacher complexity scales linearly with the keep probability $p$.

nodes.name: SGD Training with DropConnect
nodes.statement: Per-example SGD: sample mask $M$, forward propagate with masked weights, backpropagate, and update parameters.

nodes.name: Inference with DropConnect (Gaussian Moment Matching)
nodes.statement: At inference, approximate $u$ by a Gaussian via moment matching, draw $Z$ samples per unit, apply activation, and average to pass to the next layer.

nodes.name: Mean-field Inference (Hinton-style)
nodes.statement: Approximate $\sum_M a((M \star W) v) \approx a(\sum_M (M \star W) v)$ — averaging before activation rather than after; not mathematically justified for relu.

nodes.name: Logistic Loss Properties
nodes.statement: Logistic loss $A$ satisfies: (1) $A_y(0)=\ln k$; (2) $-1 \le A'_y(o) \le 1$; (3) $A''_y(o) \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Ledoux-Talagrand Contraction Lemma
nodes.statement: If $A:\mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}$ is Lipschitz with constant $L$ and $A(0)=0$, then $\hat R_\ell(A \circ H) \le 2 k L \hat R_\ell(F)$, where $H = [F_j]_{j=1}^k$ is a $k$-dimensional function class.
assumptions: $F$ is a class of real functions

nodes.name: Classifier Generalization Bound
nodes.statement: $E[A_y(o)] \le \frac{1}{\ell}\sum_{i=1}^\ell A_{y_i}(o_i) + 2k \hat R_\ell(F) + 3 \sqrt{\ln(2/\delta) / (2\ell)}$ — generalization bound for $k$-class logistic-loss classifier in terms of empirical Rademacher complexity.

nodes.name: Activation Composition Bound
nodes.statement: For all neuron activations sigmoid, tanh and relu, $\hat R_\ell(a \circ F) \le 2 \hat R_\ell(F)$.

nodes.name: Network Layer Bound
nodes.statement: Let $G = [F_j]_{j=1}^d$ and $H_B$ a linear transform parameterized by $W$ with $\|W\|_2 \le B$. Then $\hat R_\ell(H \circ G) \le \sqrt{d} B \hat R_\ell(F)$.

nodes.name: Expectation-Class Rademacher Bound
nodes.statement: Let $F_M$ be a class of real functions depending on $M$. Then $\hat R_\ell(E_M[F_M]) \le E_M[\hat R_\ell(F_M)]$.
assumptions: $F_M$ is a class of real functions parameterized by $M$

nodes.name: DropConnect Network Complexity
nodes.statement: $\hat R_\ell(F) \le p \cdot 2 \sqrt{k} d B_s n \sqrt{d} B_h \hat R_\ell(G)$ — empirical Rademacher complexity of a DropConnect network is linear in the keep probability $p$.
assumptions: $\hat R_\ell(G)$ empirical Rademacher complexity of the feature extractor
conclusions: $\hat R_\ell(F) \le p \cdot 2 \sqrt{k} d B_s n \sqrt{d} B_h \hat R_\ell(G)$

nodes.name: Layer-wise Network Bound Remark
nodes.statement: For a layer with input function class $G = [F_j]_{j=1}^d$ and linear transform $H$ with activation $a$, by Lemmas 4 and 5: $\hat R_\ell(H \circ G) \le c \sqrt{d} B \hat R_\ell(F)$, with $c=1$ for identity neuron and $c=2$ otherwise.

nodes.name: DropConnect generalizes Dropout
nodes.statement: When $a(0)=0$ (as for tanh, relu), Dropout $r = m \star a(W v) = a(m \star W v)$ — equivalent to applying a row-structured mask to $W$. DropConnect's per-entry mask is the unstructured generalization.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5 (Network Layer Bound)
nodes.statement: Expand the Rademacher supremum, use the inner-product / Cauchy-Schwarz identity to pull out $\|W\| \le B$, then bound the supremum over coordinate functions $f^j$ by a $\sqrt{d}$ factor.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6 (Expectation Bound)
nodes.statement: $\hat R_\ell(E_M[F_M]) = \hat R_\ell(\sum_M p(m) F_M) \le \sum_M \hat R_\ell(p(m) F_M) \le \sum_M |p(m)| \hat R_\ell(F_M) = E_M[\hat R_\ell(F_M)]$ by sub-additivity and homogeneity of $\hat R_\ell$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (DropConnect Complexity)
nodes.statement: Combine Lemma 6 (expectation), Lemma 4 (activation bound), Lemma 5 (linear-layer bound) and bound the diagonal-mask norm $\|D_M W\|$ by $B_h \sqrt{p \, n d}$ to obtain the linear-in-$p$ bound.

nodes.name: Bound full network by expectation over masks
nodes.statement: $\hat R_\ell(F) = \hat R_\ell(E_M[f(x;\theta,M)]) \le E_M[\hat R_\ell(f(x;\theta,M))]$ by Lemma 6.

nodes.name: Peel off softmax (linear+activation)
nodes.statement: Apply Lemmas 4 and 5 to the softmax layer to get $\hat R_\ell(F) \le 2 \sqrt{k} d B_s E_M[\hat R_\ell(h_M \circ g)]$, where $h_M = (M \star W) v$.

nodes.name: Rewrite hidden-layer Rademacher with diagonal mask
nodes.statement: $E_M[\hat R_\ell(h_M \circ g)] = E_{M,\sigma}[\sup_{h\in H, g\in G} \frac{2}{\ell} \sum_i \sigma_i W^T D_M g(x_i)]$, where $D_M$ is the diagonal matrix with diagonal $m$.

nodes.name: Bound $\|D_M W\|$ and apply layer bound
nodes.statement: Take $E_M \max \|D_M W\| \le B_h \sqrt{p\, n d}$ and bound the remaining expectation by $\sqrt{n} \hat R_\ell(G)$, giving $E_M[\hat R_\ell(h_M \circ g)] \le p n \sqrt{d} B_h \hat R_\ell(G)$.

nodes.name: Combine to obtain final bound
nodes.statement: Combining: $\hat R_\ell(F) \le p \cdot 2 \sqrt{k} d B_s n \sqrt{d} B_h \hat R_\ell(G)$.

nodes.name: Forward Pass with random mask
nodes.statement: Extract features $v \leftarrow g(x;W_g)$; sample mask $M_{ij} \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p)$; compute $r = a((M \star W) v)$ and $o = s(r;W_s)$.

nodes.name: Backpropagate gradients through masked weights
nodes.statement: Differentiate $A'_\theta$; mask the DropConnect-layer gradient: $W \leftarrow W - \eta (M \star A'_W)$. Update softmax: $W_s \leftarrow W_s - \eta A'_{W_s}$. Update feature extractor: $W_g \leftarrow W_g - \eta A'_{W_g}$.

nodes.name: Moment matching for $u$
nodes.statement: Compute $\mu \leftarrow E_M[u]$ and $\sigma^2 \leftarrow V_M[u]$ from $E_M[u]=p W v$, $V_M[u]=p(1-p)(W\star W)(v\star v)$.

nodes.name: Sample-and-activate loop
nodes.statement: For $z=1{:}Z$ and $i=1{:}d$: sample $u_{i,z} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu_i,\sigma_i^2)$; set $r_{i,z} \leftarrow a(u_{i,z})$.

nodes.name: Average samples and forward
nodes.statement: Pass result $\hat r = \sum_{z=1}^Z r_z / Z$ to the next layer.

nodes.name: MNIST classification
nodes.statement: Two fully connected 800-unit layers on MNIST with relu/sigmoid/tanh; DropConnect achieves 1.20% (relu, voting 1.12%). With deeper Ciresan-style feature extractor, DropConnect attains 0.21% error without elastic distortions, surpassing prior 0.23% state-of-the-art.

nodes.name: CIFAR-10 classification
nodes.statement: On CIFAR-10 with the larger Krizhevsky feature extractor, DropConnect achieves 11.10% per-model and 9.41% with 5-network voting; 12-network voting reaches 9.32%, beating the prior 9.5% state-of-the-art.

nodes.name: SVHN classification
nodes.statement: On the SVHN dataset (604,388 train, 26,032 test), DropConnect achieves 2.23% per-model and 1.94% with voting, improving on the previous 2.80% state-of-the-art.

nodes.name: NORB classification
nodes.statement: On the 2-fold jittered-cluttered NORB dataset (29,160 train, 58,320 test), DropConnect achieves 4.14% per-model and 3.23% with voting; both Dropout and DropConnect beat the prior 3.57% state-of-the-art.

nodes.name: GPU implementation speedup
nodes.statement: Comparing CPU vs GPU implementations of the DropConnect layer on a $4096 \times 4096$ layer with mini-batch 128: bit-packed masks in 2D-texture-aligned GPU memory yield a 414.8x speedup over a float-mask CPU baseline.
